sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Money Market**: A wholesale market for short-term debt instruments designed to meet immediate liquidity requirements of corporations, banks, and the government with maturities ranging from overnight to one year.
• **Capital Market**: A market for long-term financial assets, including equity shares and long-term bonds, facilitating capital formation, infrastructure financing, and industrial expansion.
• **Regulatory Architecture**: The **Money Market** is primarily regulated by the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**, whereas the **Capital Market** is regulated by the **Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)**.
• **Key Metric / Risk Profile**: Money market instruments carry negligible default and market risks due to high liquidity and short tenure, whereas capital market instruments carry higher market, volatility, and credit risks.

Short-term zero-coupon debt instruments issued by the Government of India in tenors of 91 days, 182 days, and 364 days.

items.title: Major Geographical Distribution / Regional Hubs
items.content:
• **Financial Capitals**: Mumbai serves as the epicenter for both capital markets (BSE, NSE, SEBI HQ) and money markets (inter-bank operations).
• **Driving Advantages**: Deep liquidity pools, robust telecommunication infrastructure, concentration of institutional investors, and proximity to policy-making bodies in Delhi and Mumbai.

items.title: Challenges, Reforms & Forward Strategy
items.content:
• **Bottlenecks / Issues**: High reliance on the banking sector, relatively shallow corporate bond market, corporate governance lapses, and retail investor hesitation.
• **Policy Interventions**: Introduction of TReDS (Trade Receivables Discounting System) for MSMEs, tightening of SEBI disclosure norms, and promotion of electronic trading platforms.

items.title: Mnemonic for Money Market Instruments
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym / Phrase**: "TC-3M" (Treasury Bills, Commercial Paper, Certificate of Deposit, Call Money, Cash Management Bills, Repo/Reverse Repo).
• **Decoded Meaning**: Covers the foundational short-term debt instruments tested in Prelims.
• **Prelims Exam Value**: Instantly helps eliminate options incorrectly attributing equity or long-term bonds to the money market.

items.title: Retention Rule of Thumb
items.content: • **Core Formula / Rule**: Money Market = Less than or equal to 364 days (RBI domain). Capital Market = Greater than 1 year to Eternity (SEBI domain).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC frequently states that 'Shares and Equities are traded in the Money Market.' This is incorrect; equities belong strictly to the capital market regardless of holding period.

Mains Value Addition: In GS-3 answers on 'Mobilization of Resources', emphasize the need to deepen the corporate bond market (capital market) to reduce systemic pressure on commercial banks (money/banking sector).

keyTakeaways: The money market manages short-term liquidity up to one year under RBI regulation, utilizing instruments like T-Bills, CPs, and CDs.
The capital market provides long-term capital for economic growth via equity and debt segments, regulated strictly by SEBI.
Distinguishing regulatory oversight, instrument maturities, and underlying risk profiles is critical for tackling both Prelims matching questions and analytical Mains prompts.
